The guided experience

Six scenes. One story.

Follow the route from the first welcome to the final recommendations. Each scene includes a photograph, English captions (CC), the history of the place and your narration audio.

SCENE 01 / 06ILLUSTRATIVE VISUAL
ENGLISH CAPTIONS

Hello, everyone! Welcome to Santa Marta, Colombia. My name is Valery, and I'll be your tour guide today. It is a pleasure to have you here. Today, we are going to explore one of the most important historical and cultural places in the city: Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino.

The entrance and first impression
01Opening · Welcome

Welcome to Santa Marta

Discover the history of this place

The estate began as La Florida San Pedro Alejandrino. The museum’s historical account dates its foundation to 2 February 1608 and names the priest Francisco de Godoy y Cortesía as its founder. The original property developed over centuries into a historic hacienda in the Santa Marta region.

Source: Fundación Museo Bolivariano, “La Quinta”.

Narration · Scene 01
SCENE 02 / 06ILLUSTRATIVE VISUAL
ENGLISH CAPTIONS

Before we start, let me explain how this experience works. First, I like to know a little about the visitors: their interests, how much time they have, and what they would like to discover. Then, I organize the tour according to their needs. We can explore the historical buildings, enjoy the gardens, and learn about the importance of this place. During the visit, I provide historical information, answer questions, and share interesting facts about the Quinta. My goal is to make this experience educational, enjoyable, and comfortable for everyone. So, are you ready to discover the history of Santa Marta?

A route designed around each visitor
02Visitor orientation · Tour guide

How the tour works

Discover the history of this place

In 1808, the estate passed to Joaquín de Mier y Benítez. Under his ownership, sugar-cane cultivation was intensified to produce panela, honey and rum. The hacienda was therefore not only a residence: it was also a productive rural enterprise whose economy shaped the property.

Source: Fundación Museo Bolivariano, “La Quinta”; Banco de la República historical research.

Narration · Scene 02
SCENE 03 / 06ILLUSTRATIVE VISUAL
ENGLISH CAPTIONS

Before we continue, let me tell you a little about the history of this wonderful place. Quinta de San Pedro Alejandrino was founded on February second, sixteen oh eight, by Francisco de Godoy y Cortesía. It was originally a traditional agricultural estate. During the nineteenth century, the estate became especially important because it was connected to the life of Simón Bolívar, known as The Liberator. He arrived here on December sixth, eighteen thirty, and sadly, he died in the main house on December seventeenth, eighteen thirty. This is why the Quinta is an important symbol of Colombian and Latin American history.

The historic house and its legacy
03Historical context · Simón Bolívar

A journey through history

Discover the history of this place

Simón Bolívar arrived at the hacienda on 6 December 1830 and died in the Main House on 17 December 1830. The principal bedroom preserves objects associated with his final days, including the bed and a clock traditionally linked to the time of his death.

Source: Fundación Museo Bolivariano, “Casa Principal” and “La Quinta”.

Narration · Scene 03
SCENE 04 / 06ILLUSTRATIVE VISUAL
ENGLISH CAPTIONS

As you can see, this place is not only about history. The Quinta also has beautiful gardens with tropical plants and impressive centenary trees, including the samán, the ceiba and the tamarind trees. The historic buildings have an ochre-yellow color, which gives the estate a very special colonial atmosphere. Another important attraction is the Bolivarian Museum of Contemporary Art, where visitors can discover different works of art from Colombia and other countries. We can also find the Altar de la Patria, a monument created to honor the memory of Simón Bolívar.

A living collection of history and nature
04Heritage · Nature · Contemporary art

Architecture, gardens and art

Discover the history of this place

The gardens preserve centenary trees such as the samán, ceiba and tamarind, alongside plants associated with the tropical dry-forest ecosystem of the Caribbean region. The estate’s historic value is therefore connected to both cultural memory and living natural heritage.

Source: Fundación Museo Bolivariano, “La Quinta”.

Listening, adapting and helping
05Guest care · Practical dialogue

Visitor assistance and problem solving

Discover the history of this place

The Bolivarian Museum of Contemporary Art opened on 24 July 1986. It grew from an initiative led by artist Armando Villegas, with the aim of expressing cultural links among the countries associated with Bolívar through contemporary art.

Source: Fundación Museo Bolivariano, “Museo Bolivariano de Arte Contemporáneo”.

A thoughtful ending to the visit
06Visitor recommendations · Closing

Recommendations and farewell

Discover the history of this place

After Joaquín de Mier’s family ownership, the Department of Magdalena acquired the estate in 1891 with the stated purpose of preserving it. In 1959, it was declared a National Historical Monument under Law 163. These milestones helped establish its role as a site of public heritage.

Source: Fundación Museo Bolivariano; ICOMOS Colombia, national heritage record.

Visitor information

Essential context for visitors and a practical reference for the guide. Opening hours and admission information below were checked against the institution’s published 2026 information.

A place of history and memory

The Quinta brings together the historic hacienda, the memory of Simón Bolívar, a botanical garden and contemporary art collections.

Historical timeline
2 Feb 1608The estate was founded by Francisco de Godoy y Cortesía under the name La Florida de San Pedro Alejandrino.
6 Dec 1830Simón Bolívar arrived at the estate, according to the historical account presented by the museum.
17 Dec 1830Simón Bolívar died in the Main House.
2 Feb 1891The Department of Magdalena acquired the estate for its preservation.
1959The estate was declared a National Historical Monument under Law 163 of 1959.
24 Jul 1986The Bolivarian Museum of Contemporary Art opened inside the estate.
What visitors can discover
  • The Main House and rooms connected with Bolívar’s final days.
  • The old colonial bridge and ochre-yellow historic buildings.
  • The botanical garden and centenary trees, including the samán, ceiba and tamarind.
  • The Bolivarian Museum of Contemporary Art and the Altar de la Patria.

Before you arrive

A comfortable visit begins with a little preparation. Check access and current operating conditions before travelling.

Practical recommendations
  • Wear comfortable walking shoes and clothing suitable for a warm tropical climate.
  • Bring water and sun protection for the outdoor areas.
  • Allow enough time for the house, gardens and museum collections you wish to visit.
  • Buy admission tickets at the museum ticket office unless the institution confirms another arrangement.
  • For a short visit, ask staff which areas are open and prioritize the places that matter most to you.
Conservation and visitor rules
  • Do not use flash inside exhibition rooms.
  • Do not touch artworks, historical objects or monuments.
  • Do not walk on lawns or climb trees.
  • Food and drinks are not permitted inside enclosed museum rooms.
  • Large backpacks and packages may not be allowed in the galleries.
  • Children must remain with a responsible adult.
  • Pets are restricted from indoor rooms; the museum lists leash requirements for open areas.
  • Entry to the woodland area requires an institutional guide.
  • Follow staff instructions and posted signs; access rules may change by area or exhibition.
